conventions.axes: Y-up, right-handed; camera looks down -Z by default; ground is the XZ plane at y = 0
conventions.lightIntensity: three.js physical units (directional/hemisphere/ambient: lux-like; spot/point: candela, decay 2)
conventions.easing: named functions from kit/time.js `ease` (formulas in references/kit-api.md)
conventions.camera: fov is vertical field of view in degrees (three.js convention); sensor-agnostic

style.name: Impossible Geometry
style.description: Sunlit pastel-stone architecture under an orthographic camera that lies: a real open staircase whose two ends line up from one magic angle into an endless loop, with a little walker climbing for ever, then the camera swings off-axis and the loop splits open to show the trick. Flat three-tone faces, fine edge lines, a soft ground shadow, a calm sky.
motion: The camera holds still on the magic view while the walker climbs; one slow orbit (path 'arc') swings 30-45 deg off it to reveal the gap, then returns and the loop seals.
The walker hops one step at a time on a fixed clock (stand, then a quick arc); at the top it steps onto the bottom step — a teleport along the view direction.
Nothing else moves: the architecture is stone; the flag ripples on the same clock as the steps.

scene.notes: A Penrose-style staircase built as a REAL open chain (impossible.penroseStairs): flights of 7/3/3/7 steps whose closing step lands exactly k·v from the first step, v = the magic orthographic view direction. The far end of the chain is cut in-shader where it lies between the first steps and their virtual copy (the seam), so from the magic view the loop is seamless; the cut fades out off-axis. The walker's position is closed-form from t (impossible.walkerAt); footsteps are a Shepard marimba (one octave per lap) from the same step list.
